items.headline: Lebanon Fragile Hold Hour ~180+ — Hezbollah 'Null And Void' Rubio Framework June 27; IDF Drone June 27; No Void Activation Overnight; G7 Coordination Pending
items.summary: Lebanon enters Hour ~180+ of the nominally operative ceasefire framework under maximum stress. Hezbollah Secretary-General issued a statement June 27 declaring the Rubio framework 'null and void,' citing IDF failure to withdraw from agreed buffer zone coordinates by the June 27 deadline. The 'null and void' language is the formal trigger phrase for ceasefire dissolution — its appearance is the highest-severity precursor signal in the Lebanon monitoring arc since the ceasefire's implementation. As of June 30 morning, the declaration has not been operationalized: no IDF strike response, no Hezbollah rocket barrage, no formal void notification to the UN. IDF drone activity June 27 in southern Lebanon was characterized by IDF as surveillance; Hezbollah disputed this. No Lebanon events overnight June 29-30. G7 allied response to the June 28 Iran missile strikes is being coordinated through Geneva diplomatic channels; Lebanon's fragility complicates G7 unified positioning on the combined Iran-Lebanon threat arc.

items.headline: CRITICAL: Tucannon Fire Day 3 — ~15,000 Acres Garfield County; Zero Containment; Record Fuel Dryness; Agricultural Interface Risk; East Cascades Onset Day 3; NIFC Morning Update Pending
items.summary: The Tucannon Fire in Garfield County, southeastern Washington enters Day 3 at approximately 15,000 acres — the largest active fire in the Pacific Northwest and the most significant ignition of the East Cascades onset window (Day 3). Ignited in the Tucannon River drainage area, expanded aggressively under record fuel moisture deficits — eastern Washington shrub-steppe fuel moisture readings are the lowest on NIFC record for this calendar date, running 12-15 days ahead of historical fire onset schedule. No meaningful overnight containment progress reported. The Garfield County position places the fire in the eastern Palouse/Blue Mountains agricultural-wildland interface — wheat harvest season is now active in eastern Washington; standing grain fields in the interface zone represent atypical fuel continuity and significant economic secondary risk if fire runs northward into the Palouse cropping zone. Aerial resources are available following the Kartar Fire's June 27 100% containment. NIFC morning daily update (~6-8 AM PDT) is the first authoritative Day 3 size and containment estimate. Second PNW heat wave: a high-pressure dome has reestablished over the region, driving temperatures 95-105°F along the I-5 corridor and 100°F+ across the Columbia Basin, including the Tucannon Fire area (RH 5-12%). Peak fire weather window June 30 - July 2. BPA grid is stressed from heat wave demand spike compounding the drought-year-4 hydropower constraint — second consecutive heat wave in 15 days against the lowest Columbia River flows since 2001.

items.headline: OBBB SIGNED Day 1 — VP Vance 50-50; 218-214 House; Watson v. RNC Day 1 Mail Ballot Grace Periods Eliminated; Trump Mail-In EO Day 1; SCOTUS Humphrey's Executor Morning Window
items.summary: Three major June 29 evening domestic developments reshape the political and legal landscape entering June 30 morning. First: the OBBB — One Big Beautiful Bill, branded Reconciliation 2.0 — was signed into law by President Trump on June 29 following the 50-50 VP Vance tie-break in the Senate and 218-214 House passage. Day 1 of OBBB implementation. The legislative arc that began with Speaker Johnson's January reconciliation commitment — complicated by Freedom Caucus spending demands, Medicaid work requirements, SALT cap negotiations, and Byrd Rule challenges across multiple missed floor date signals — is complete. The signed bill is the single largest fiscal legislation since the 2021 American Rescue Plan. Second: Watson v. RNC, decided 5-4 for the Republican National Committee, eliminates mail-in ballot grace periods in all 50 states effective immediately. Ballots must arrive by Election Day close; postmark-only rules are invalidated. The ruling has immediate November 2026 midterm implications — state election administrators have a September preparation deadline for absentee ballot procedures across all 50 states. Trump's concurrent mail-in voting Executive Order operationalizes Watson's ruling at the federal election administration level. Third: SCOTUS final morning opinion window — Humphrey's Executor v. United States is the outstanding case of highest consequence; an overturn of the 1935 precedent would eliminate presidential removal constraints on independent agency heads at FTC, NLRB, SEC, CFPB, FDIC. SCOTUS opinions typically release ~10 AM PDT. No ruling as of 7 AM.

items.headline: Measles Day 11 CLEAN — Both Lumen Field Windows Final Checkpoint; CIDRAP Slowing Streak Intact; NSF Newport OR Removal Day 2; Cascadia Monitoring Gap Active
items.summary: Three secondary PNW threads. First: measles dual incubation window surveillance advances to Day 11 CLEAN — both Lumen Field exposure events at their final cluster identification checkpoint. June 15 match (16 days post-exposure) and June 19 match (12 days post-exposure) have cleared their primary cluster emergence period with no confirmed new cases attributable to either event. King County and Snohomish County DOH morning reports show no cluster alerts. The CIDRAP slowing signal streak is intact. National case count holds at 2,073 (CDC June 11). Next CDC interim update expected July 9. Georgetown University fusion surveillance (wastewater DNA, ER visit rates, social media symptom mapping) providing the operative monitoring mechanism through close of the June 19 window. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatories — scheduled removal from the Oregon coast Cascadia Subduction Zone real-time monitoring network completed approximately June 28. June 30 morning marks Day 2 of the Cascadia offshore seismic monitoring gap. No federal replacement plan announced. No Cascadia Subduction Zone seismic events recorded since removal. The monitoring gap is now operational with no interim coverage mechanism confirmed. Third: Washington drought emergency Day 26 (4th consecutive drought year, sub-50% snowpack, Columbia River at 2001-era lows). Oregon EO 26-10 Day 15. No precipitation relief projected through July 4.
